grade.basis: Independent review of all four complete-score pages: Allegro moderato quarter=100, scalar eighths and sixteenths with short slurs, repeated detached notes and dotted-sixteenth figures in tenor clef, reaching the upper tenor register; the Lento quarter=60 requires sustained cantabile and controlled upper-register shifts. Cello 2 briefly reaches high ledger notes too, but cello 1 combines the sustained upper tessitura and most active repeated-note lead writing. Short scale patterns and lack of extensive chords or virtuoso passagework support early advanced, without an ensemble uplift. Advisory estimate within one level, not exhaustive note certification.

findings.finding: Visually reviewed score pp.1–4, including the tenor-clef Allegro material, Lento and D.C. al Fine; grade reflects the actual four-cello notation.

grade.basis: Independent visual review of the complete 24-bar G-major Prelude score and all four parts (PDF pp.1–8). At quarter=56 the semiquavers and occasional demisemiquavers are controlled rather than rapid; cello 1 stays unusually high in bass-clef ledger notation, with chromatic shifts, paired slurs, separate up-bows, ornaments and a final ascending run. Cello 3 has substantial flowing string-crossing figures but a lower tessitura. The upper-register intonation and bow articulation place the hardest individual part at early advanced; brief duration limits stamina demands. No automatic counterpoint/ensemble uplift. Advisory within one level.

findings.finding: Actual Dicker PDF 952243 reviewed in full: Prelude XIX only, G major, quarter=56, score plus cello 1–4 parts; highest sustained register and closing ascent belong to cello 1.

grade.basis: Independent review of all 11 pages of the actual Mandozzi transcription, theme through variation XX. Cello 1 remains largely in tenor clef and bears rapid separate-bow semiquaver arpeggios, wide register/string crossings, repeated figuration, trills and upper-register shifting; variation XVIII explicitly allows easier substitute arpeggios, but this grade takes the printed principal version. Cello 2 is comparably active in the final variations and cello 3 has demanding running bass variations. Sustaining the leading part over the whole variation chain at convincing Allegro/Vivace tempi makes pre-diploma plausible without requiring a professional level. No grade imported from the violin original and no ensemble uplift. Advisory within one level.

findings.finding: Complete 3-cello Mandozzi score visually reviewed, pp.1–11; hardest printed figuration includes variations XVIII–XX and the final alternating running passages.

grade.basis: Independent visual review of the complete Version A score, all three blues movements (PDF pp.4–28, printed pp.1–25). The hardest combined demands fall in viola 4: Loekie Blues includes exposed chromatic rising figures and a brief excursion above the treble staff around bars 79–83; Slow Blues Song adds active chromatic semiquaver figures with mixed slurred and detached articulation; De Stille requires crisp offbeat attacks, chromatic runs and occasional four-note tuplets at dotted-quarter=124. Much of the set is simpler, but the peak register and clean rapid articulation support advanced rather than an average of all eight parts. Repetition requires sustained rhythmic discipline, while rests reduce endurance pressure. No automatic eight-player uplift. Medium advisory estimate within one level; not exhaustive note certification.

findings.finding: Reviewed all 28 PDF pages of the eight-viola Version A, including Loekie Blues (dotted-quarter=116), Slow Blues Song (66), and De Stille (124). Whole set assessed; no clarinet-choir or mixed-string notation used. Blues/modal mixture makes a single major/minor label uncertain.
